body.statement:
Under overlap, bounded outcomes, bounded aspect ratio, propensity-path stability, the primitive oracle gap, and \(b_{nm}=o(1)\),
\[
 Z^{\mathrm B}=Z^{\bar p}+D^{\mathrm B}+R^{\mathrm B},\qquad
 E_P[Z^{\bar p}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]=M^{\mathrm B}_{ij}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \lVert R^{\mathrm B}\rVert=O_P(Bq^{-3}\log(en)).
\]
Writing
\[
 a^{\mathrm B,loose}_{nm}=\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\left[1\wedge
 \frac B{\lambda_{nm}}\left\{
 q^{-1}\sqrt{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}+q^{-3}\log(en)
 \right\}\right],
\]
the blind fit obeys \(\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U^{\mathrm B})=O_P(a^{\mathrm B,loose}_{nm})\).  The frozen assumptions do not imply the sharper claim that the residual contributes \(o_P(b_{nm})\) to maximum-row loss.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(t_i=\widehat p_i-\bar p_i\) and \(s_i=1-\bar p_i\).  The exact reciprocal identities
\[
 \frac1{\bar p_i+t_i}=\frac1{\bar p_i}-\frac{t_i}{\bar p_i^2}
 +\frac{t_i^2}{\bar p_i^2(\bar p_i+t_i)},
\]
and
\[
 \frac1{s_i-t_i}=\frac1{s_i}+\frac{t_i}{s_i^2}
 +\frac{t_i^2}{s_i^2(s_i-t_i)}
\]
give the asserted decomposition with
\[
\begin{aligned}
 R^{\mathrm B}_{ij}
 &=-t_i\{Q_{ij}-H^{\mathrm B}_{ij}\}+t_i^2S_{ij},\\
 Q_{ij}&=\frac{A_{ij}Y_{ij}}{\bar p_i^2}
 +\frac{(1-A_{ij})Y_{ij}}{(1-\bar p_i)^2},\\
 S_{ij}&=\frac{A_{ij}Y_{ij}}{\bar p_i^2\widehat p_i}
 -\frac{(1-A_{ij})Y_{ij}}{(1-\bar p_i)^2(1-\widehat p_i)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
All denominators are bounded away from zero: \(\bar p_i\in[q,1-q]\) and \(\widehat p_i\in[q/2,1-q/2]\).  Sequential randomization gives
\(E_P[Q_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]=H^{\mathrm B}_{ij}\), so \(Q-H^{\mathrm B}\) is a bounded matrix martingale-difference array.  Self-adjoint dilation and the cited matrix Freedman inequality give
\[
 \lVert Q-H^{\mathrm B}\rVert
 =O_P\!\left(Bq^{-2}\sqrt{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}
 +Bq^{-2}\log(e(n+m))\right).
\]
The tangent-control lemma gives \(\max_i|t_i|=O_P(\sqrt{\log(en)/m})\), while \(\max_{ij}|S_{ij}|\le CBq^{-3}\).  Since left multiplication by \(\operatorname{diag}(t_i)\) has operator norm \(\max_i|t_i|\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \lVert R^{\mathrm B}\rVert
 &\le \max_i|t_i|\,\lVert Q-H^{\mathrm B}\rVert
 +CBq^{-3}\sqrt{nm}\max_i t_i^2\\
 &=O_P(Bq^{-3}\log(en)),
\end{aligned}
\]
where bounded aspect ratio absorbs the smaller logarithmic and rectangular factors.

The conditional mean assertion follows separately from
\[
 E_P[Z^{\bar p}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]
 =\frac{p_{ij}\mu^1_{ij}}{\bar p_i}
 -\frac{(1-p_{ij})\mu^0_{ij}}{1-\bar p_i}=M^{\mathrm B}_{ij}.
\]
The centered array \(Z^{\bar p}-M^{\mathrm B}\) has increments bounded by \(CB/q\) and conditional second moments bounded by \(CB^2/q^2\).  Matrix Freedman thus gives
\[
 \lVert Z^{\bar p}-M^{\mathrm B}\rVert
 =O_P\!\left(Bq^{-1}\sqrt{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}
 +Bq^{-1}\log(e(n+m))\right).
\]
Combining this with the residual bound controls
\(Z^{\mathrm B}-T^{\mathrm B}\).  Tangent control supplies a gap at least \((c_{\mathrm B}/2)\lambda_{nm}\) with probability tending to one.  Repeating the singular-equation and polar-factor argument from the loose IPW theorem, now around \(T^{\mathrm B}\), yields
\[
 \mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U^{\mathrm B})
 \le C\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left(1\wedge\frac{\lVert Z^{\mathrm B}-T^{\mathrm B}\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}}\right)
 =O_P(a^{\mathrm B,loose}_{nm}).
\]
This proof uses only operator perturbation.  It does not convert an endogenous future singular factor into a predictable martingale weight, which is precisely why it does not yield the originally asserted \(b_{nm}\) rowwise rate.
